challenge.name: Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data
challenge.objective: Build an SI-powered, web-based dashboard that summarizes, ranks and interprets combustion science investigations to deliver foundational fire-safety insights for human space exploration.
challenge.outOfScope: Rocket and propellant fire safety: rocket-engine combustion is effectively independent of gravity and generally beyond PSI's research.

facts: PSI contains NO partial-gravity (lunar 0.16 g / Martian 0.38 g) combustion data. LUCI and FM2 may add it in future. Lunar/Martian statements are theoretical bounds between microgravity and 1 g results.
E-FIELD Flames mimicked partial gravity with electric fields: an analogue, not real partial gravity.
CFI-G's up-to-85% O2 was a burner stream into a nitrogen + fuel chamber, not a cabin atmosphere.
Expected lunar habitat/rover atmosphere: >=30% O2 at <=10.2 psi. Spacesuit: 100% O2 at 4.3 psi. Earth sea level and ISS: 21% O2 at 14.7 psi.
Spacecraft fire safety = prevention (ignition control, material selection via flammability limits), detection, suppression.
Rocket/propellant fire safety is out of scope.

hardware.desc: Droplet-combustion facility inside the CIR. FLEX, FLEX-2 and the Cool Flames Investigation (CFI) all burned liquid fuel droplets with it.

hardware.name: ACME modular hardware (in the CIR)
hardware.desc: Shared modular hardware for the six ACME experiments, all flames of gaseous fuels.

hardware.name: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) flow duct
hardware.desc: Modular fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE and used inside the MSG by BASS, BASS-II, SPICE and SLICE, covering solid and gaseous fuels. Thermo team reference: low-speed flow up to ~40 cm/s, opposed and concurrent flow.

hardware.name: Cygnus cargo vehicle (Saffire)
hardware.desc: Saffire-I, -II and -III ran large-scale material burns inside an uncrewed Cygnus resupply vehicle after it left the ISS. Thermo team reference: sample cards up to 0.94 m × 0.4 m; thermocouples, radiometers, O₂/CO₂ and pressure telemetry. Configurations differ between Saffire-I, II and III.

hardware.name: ISS smoke & aerosol diagnostics
hardware.desc: Smoke-particle measurement instruments for fire detection (SAME, SAME-R). One SAME instrument (the TSI P-Trak) was tested for dust in DAFT / DAFT-2.

models.description: Computes constant-pressure adiabatic flame temperature (T_ad) and equilibrium product species mole fractions across reduced-pressure, oxygen-enriched exploration atmospheres (e.g., 10.2 psi / 30% O2 lunar habitat vs. 14.7 psi / 21% O2 ISS).

Evaluates mixture thermal diffusivity (alpha), binary mass diffusivity (D_im), and effective Lewis number (Le = alpha / D_im) for fuel/O2/inert mixtures (N2, CO2, He) to quantify preferential diffusion and thermo-diffusive flame ball instabilities in 0g.

Determines the conserved scalar stoichiometric mixture fraction (Z_st) and theoretical spherical flame-sheet radius ratio (r_f / r_b) for both normal diffusion flames and 'inside-out' inverse flames (oxygen jet into fuel-diluent ambient).
Calculates instantaneous Heat Release Rate Q_dot(t) [kW] and integrated total heat release [kJ] from forced-flow duct exhaust gas analyzers during large-scale spacecraft material burn tests.
Predicts steady flame spread velocity (V_f) against an opposing low-speed cabin ventilation flow (0.5-40 cm/s) across solid fabrics (cotton/Sibal, Nomex) and plastics (PMMA) in microgravity.
Models flow-assisted (concurrent) flame propagation where forced cabin airflow sweeps hot combustion gases downstream over unburned solid fuel, driving accelerating pyrolysis lengths.
Computes the critical high-velocity convective blow-off limit where forced ventilation sweeps heat and radicals out of the flame leading edge faster than chemical reactions can replenish them.

Quantifies the ratio of buoyancy-driven natural convection to forced cabin ventilation across 0g (ISS), 0.16g (Moon), 0.38g (Mars), and 1g (Earth) to establish theoretical partial-gravity flammability bounds.
Computes the dimensionless Spalding mass-transfer driving force (B-number) and surface gasification mass flux (m''_f) for solid polymers (PMMA, silicone) and cellulosic fabrics.
Simulates spherically symmetric isolated liquid fuel droplet burning (methanol, n-heptane, n-octane, n-decane) in microgravity, solving squared diameter regression D^2(t) and burning rate constant K.

Predicts two-stage combustion in large alkane droplets (n-heptane, n-octane, n-decane) where a visible hot flame radiatively extinguishes into an invisible, low-temperature 'cool flame' before final diffusive extinction.
Models vapor-liquid equilibrium and preferential evaporation in multicomponent or water-absorbing droplets (e.g., methanol droplets absorbing combustion-generated water vapor in 0g).
Determines the fundamental low-velocity radiative quenching limit (< 1-2 cm/s) where diffusive oxygen transport is too slow to offset gas-phase and surface thermal radiation losses.
Quantifies the radiative heat loss fraction (chi_r = Q_dot_rad / Q_dot_total) of microgravity solid and gaseous fires from directional radiometer measurements and flame geometry.
Predicts whether a microgravity diffusion flame burns as a dim, blue soot-free flame or transitions to a luminous yellow sooting flame based on thermal gradients and residence time.
Models transient solid-phase heating, thermal penetration depth, and time-to-ignition (t_ign) of spacecraft cabin polymers and textiles exposed to an external radiative/convective heat flux.

Solves for the microgravity Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI_0g) — the minimum ambient O2 mole fraction required to sustain flame propagation — contrasting it against Earth 1g upward-burn standards (NASA-STD-6001).
Evaluates the thermodynamic extinguishing efficacy of spacecraft fire suppression agents (CO2, N2, He, fine water mist) by quantifying heat-sink capacity vs. conductive heat loss.
Predicts transient cabin pressure rise (delta-P), bulk gas temperature, O2 depletion, and CO2 toxicity buildup during a fire inside a sealed spacecraft module, Lunar habitat, or pressurized rover.

Models smoke particle agglomeration and transport velocity to spacecraft fire detectors in microgravity, where absence of buoyant plumes increases particle residence time and alters size distributions.

iss.label: ISS cabin
iss.significance: No buoyancy; burning controlled by forced ventilation (team reference: 5–40 cm/s) and molecular diffusion.

lunar_habitat.label: Lunar habitat / pressurized rover
lunar_habitat.gravity: 0.16 g — NO PSI DATA (theoretical bound only)
lunar_habitat.note: Expected conditions per the challenge brief.
lunar_habitat.significance: Lower pressure reduces convective cooling and diluent heat capacity while more O₂ raises flame temperature and spread rate. Chosen to shorten EVA pre-breathing.

spacesuit.label: Spacesuit
spacesuit.significance: Pure oxygen removes the nitrogen heat sink: very easy ignition and rapid flame spread.

earth.label: Earth sea level (1 g baseline)
earth.significance: Buoyant plume draws in fresh O₂ (team reference: ~30–50 cm/s). Baseline for NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 upward-burn screening.

futureExperiments.name: LUCI — Lunar-g Combustion Investigation
futureExperiments.desc: Expected future source of partial-gravity combustion data.

futureExperiments.name: FM2 — Flammability of Materials on the Moon
futureExperiments.desc: First combustion experiment on another planetary body; burns materials at lunar 1/6 g.

futureExperiments.name: SoFIE — Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
futureExperiments.desc: ISS investigation of fire growth; motivated by concern that NASA-STD-6001's 1 g test is not conservative in low g.

futureExperiments.name: FLARE — Flammability Limits At Reduced-g Experiment
futureExperiments.desc: Method to estimate microgravity flammability limits from ground tests; JAXA, NASA, ESA, CNES, DLR and universities.
